header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jenna Lee (Aurora - Head of MLOps), Carlos Mendes (Aurora - CTO), Priya Shah (Aurora - Platform Eng), Martin Cole (Aurora - Product Ops)
Meeting ID: rwd-aurora-qbr-2026-07-08-01
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining for the QBR. Quick check—can you hear me okay?
[00:00:05] Jenna (Head of MLOps): Yep loud and clear.
[00:00:07] Carlos (CTO): Good to go.
[00:00:10] Maya: Awesome. Agenda — we have usage and cost trends, a quick recap of the reliability incident in May, dedicated vs private options, security docs, and then next steps. Samir will jump into the benchmark numbers.
[00:00:25] Samir (SE): Hi all, thanks. I'll start with the usage slide — high level: Aurora saw 2.1B tokens in the quarter, about 45% increase q/q, embeddings are now ~28% of total cost due to higher semantic search usage.
[00:00:45] Priya (Platform Eng): That matches what we saw—search queries spiked after the marketing campaign. The embeddings pipeline is our biggest surprise.
[00:00:55] Maya: Right, embeddings at scale can be a significant driver. We recommended batching and cache TTLs last quarter; have you been able to tune those?
[00:01:05] Jenna: We implemented batching but haven't enabled prefix caching extensively because of session semantics. There's a KV cache we could leverage more but worried about staleness.
[00:01:18] Samir: Understood. We can set up a conservative TTL for prefix cache to start and measure hit rates. That often cuts token spend by 20-30% without impacting freshness too much.
[00:01:30] Carlos: Walk me through dedicated vs private—what's the delta on cost and latency?
[00:01:35] Maya: For Dedicated (reserved capacity) you get predictable throughput — you can size the GPU pool. Per-token unit cost is lower than hosted burst pricing once you commit. Private (VPC/on-prem) adds networking and infra overhead but gives full data-plane control and can meet stricter compliance. Latency: Dedicated usually gives better tail latency than multi-tenant hosted, Private depends on your infra.
[00:01:57] Martin (Product Ops): We're leaning Private for data residency plus SSO integration. How heavy is the networking setup?
[00:02:05] Samir: The Private deployment needs a VPN or Direct Connect-style link if on cloud; for on-prem we provide an appliance package. There's an initial setup window — usually 4-6 weeks for networking and KMS integration.
[00:02:18] Jenna: And audits? SOC2?
[00:02:21] Maya: Yes, we have SOC2 + ISO attestations. We'll send the attestations and the compliance FAQ. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) and we keep audit logs at token-level in the Console.
[00:02:33] Priya: Do you support SAML SSO + RBAC for team roles?
[00:02:36] Samir: Yes, SAML SSO and granular RBAC. We can map roles to routes and models.
[00:02:42] [00:03:00] Speaker 2: Sorry jumping in—on the May outage, can you summarize root cause again?
[00:03:05] Maya: Sure — brief recap: a kernel regression in an optimized attention path impacted a subset of models under a specific sequence-length distribution during autoscaling. We had fallbacks to a compatible model variant, but it increased latency. Post-mortem: fixed the regression, added additional canary checks for kernel builds and tightened the autoscale cooldown.
[00:03:30] Carlos: Latency spike was painful for users—are there guarantees?
[00:03:33] Samir: We provide SLAs for Dedicated customers. For hosted, we have SLOs and we always recommend a fallback policy and model variants pinned for critical routes. Also multi-region routing helps.
[00:03:45] Jenna: For our critical route, we need p99 under 450ms. Can Dedicated meet that?
[00:03:50] Samir: Yes, with the right instance type and batch sizing you can hit sub-300ms p99 for many models. We'll run a benchmark with your top-10 prompts and aim to publish p50/p95/p99 numbers.
[00:04:05] [00:04:15] Maya: Quick pause — Carlos, what's your timeline decision for Dedicated vs Private?
[00:04:20] Carlos: Prefer Dedicated to start in Q3 to get predictability, then migrate to Private by late Q4 if residency and audit windows require.
[00:04:29] Priya: If we go Dedicated first, will it be easy to migrate to Private?
[00:04:32] Samir: Yes—we expose the same API and rollout tooling. Migration is mostly infra and networking; model versions and configs port over.
[00:04:40] [00:05:00] Jenna: Cost questions — can you break down the big ticket items?
[00:05:04] Samir: Sure — large drivers are token generation (long contexts), embeddings, and model family choice (quantized Llama variants vs larger dense models). Options: quantization profiles, batching, and prefix caching. Also consider model family substitutions for lower cost with similar quality.
[00:05:22] Martin: Any quick numbers for tradeoff? Like cost delta if we quantize to int8?
[00:05:26] Samir: It's workload dependent but ballpark 30-50% compute cost reduction with small accuracy tradeoffs. We'll run your prompts to quantify.
[00:05:35] [00:06:00] Speaker 1 (Maya): Okay, next — runbook and ops. You've had two incidents this quarter; what's your ops playbook?
[00:06:07] Jenna: We have a pager for the app tier; Redwood incidents reached product eng. We want clearer alerting from the Redwood Console on per-route token cost spikes and failed model fallbacks.
[00:06:18] Samir: Good feedback — we can push route-level alerting and add webhook integrations to your PagerDuty. Also we'll surface fallback events in the trace view.
[00:06:29] Priya: Will that include KV cache hit rates?
[00:06:31] Samir: Yes, cache hit/miss metrics are available; we can add an alert if hit rate drops below threshold.
[00:06:38] [00:06:55] Carlos: About data retention—how long are logs kept by default and can we control retention for privacy?
[00:07:00] Maya: Default retention is 90 days for hosted; for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and we support route-level redaction. We'll include details in the compliance pack.
[00:07:10] [00:07:30] Samir: On the private networking deep-dive — we'd like to include your infra and networking folks in that session; it's typically a design call where we map out VPC routes, KMS endpoints, and egress controls.
[00:07:43] Jenna: We'll invite our network lead.
[00:07:45] [00:08:00] Martin: One last business question—pricing model for embeddings at scale. Can you tier it?
[00:08:07] Maya: We can provide committed usage tiers which substantially lower embedding unit price. That's part of the reserved capacity proposal we'll send.
[00:08:15] [00:08:40] Speaker 2 (Customer): Also curious about multi-region failover for GDPR—any gotchas?
[00:08:44] Samir: We support region pinning and can set up read replicas. For GDPR, data residency is enforced by keeping the data plane in-region with Private deployments or dedicated regional deployments. We'll document specifics for Aurora.
[00:08:58] [00:09:20] Maya: Alright, quick recap of agreed items: Maya sends pricing + reserved capacity proposal; Samir sends SOC2/ISO and runs benchmark; Aurora sends Q3 traffic and prompt set; schedule networking deep-dive. Anything to add?
[00:09:33] Jenna: That covers it. Thanks.
[00:09:36] Carlos: Thanks everyone.
[00:09:40] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up over email.
[00:09:45] [END OF RECORDING — transcript truncated for brevity]
